{{Short description|German mathematician (1873–1942)}}
[[File: Rudolf Ernst Rothe.jpg|thumb|{{center|Rudolf Ernst Rothe}}]]
'''Rudolf Ernst Rothe''' (15 October 1873 in [[Berlin]] – 26 October 1942 in Berlin)<ref>biographical data, session reports of the ''Berliner Mathematischen Gesellschaft'' (Berlin Mathematical Society), 2001</ref> was a German applied mathematician.<ref name="Emmer2003">{{cite book|editor=Emmer, Michele|chapter=''Mathematics and fascism. The case of Berlin'' by Jochen Brüning|title=Mathematics and Culture I|chapter-url=https://books.google.com/books?id=EHRDnU29PO8C&q=rothe&pg=PA16|date=2 December 2003|publisher=Springer Science & Business Media|isbn=978-3-540-01770-7|postscript=; translated from the original Italian of ''Matematica e culture 2000'' by Emanuela Moreale}}</ref>

==Biography==
After graduating from the Sophien-Gymnasium in Berlin, Rothe studied from 1892 under [[Hermann Amandus Schwarz]], [[Johannes Knoblauch]], [[Lazarus Immanuel Fuchs]], and [[Ferdinand Georg Frobenius]]<ref>He mentions these mathematicians as particularly formative in the appendix to his dissertation.</ref> at the [[Humboldt University of Berlin]]. There in 1897 he received his [[Promotion (Germany)|''Promotion'']] (Ph.D.) with dissertation ''Untersuchungen über die Theorie der isothermal Flächen'' (Investigations on the theory of isothermal surfaces) supervised by Schwarz. In 1905 Rothe completed his [[habilitation]] at the ''Technische Hochschule Berlin-Charlottenburg'' (now [[Technische Universität Berlin]]). He was a professor from 1908 to 1914 at the [[Clausthal University of Technology]] (TU Claustral) and from 1914 to 1915 at the ''Technische Hochschule Hanover'' ([[University of Hanover]]), where he founded the Institute for Applied Mathematics. From 1915 he was a professor at ''Technische Hochschule Berlin'', where he was rector in 1921. After retiring in 1939, he was an honorary senator of Technische Universität Berlin.

His research deals with differential geometry and function theory. During WW I, he did research on [[ballistics]] and on determining the trajectories for the projectiles fired from the "[[Paris gun]]" (which in 1918 was fired at Paris from 120 kilometers away).<ref>{{cite book|editor=Hermann, Armin|editor2=Sang, Hans Peter|title=Technik und Staat|publisher=VDI Verlag|year=1992|page=368}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|author=Grüß, Gerhard|title=Rudolf Rothe zum Gedächtnis|journal=Zeitschrift für Angewandte Mathematik und Mechanik|volume=22|issue=5|year=1942|page=302|doi=10.1002/zamm.19420220522|bibcode=1942ZaMM...22..302G}}</ref>

In 1926 he was elected a member of the [[German National Academy of Sciences Leopoldina]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Rudolf Rothe|website=Nationale Akademie der Wissenschafter Leopoldnia|url=https://www.leopoldina.org/mitglieder/mitgliederverzeichnis/mitglieder/member/Member/show/5091/}}</ref>

In 1930 he was president of the [[German Mathematical Society|''Deutsche Mathematiker-Vereinigung'']]. From 1916 to 1918 and from 1939 to 1941 he was chair of the Berlin Mathematical Society, of which he was a founding member.

After the death of [[Johannes Knoblauch]], Rothe completed the editing and publishing of the collected works of [[Karl Weierstrass]]. Rothe was co-editor with [[Felix Auerbach]] of the ''Taschenbuch für Mathematiker und Physiker'' (Pocket-sized book for mathematicians and physicists), published by ''[[B. G. Teubner Verlag]]'' in 1911<ref name="Ponzer1912">{{cite journal|last1=Ponzer|first1=Ernest W.|title=Book Review: ''Taschenbuch für Mathematiker und Physiker''|journal=Bulletin of the American Mathematical Society|volume=19|issue=1|year=1912|pages=21–23|issn=0002-9904|doi=10.1090/S0002-9904-1912-02286-3|doi-access=free}}</ref> and 1913<ref name="AuerbachRothe1913">{{cite book|editor1=Felix Auerbach|editor2=Rudolf Rothe|title=Taschenbuch für Mathematiker und Physiker|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=ao4eAQAAMAAJ|year=1913|publisher=B. G. Teubner.}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|last1=Miller|first1=G. A.|author-link=George Abram Miller|title=Book Review: ''Taschenbuch für Mathematiker und Physiker''|journal=Bulletin of the American Mathematical Society|volume=20|issue=4|year=1914|pages=201–203|issn=0002-9904|doi=10.1090/S0002-9904-1914-02465-6|doi-access=free}}</ref> (and first published in 1909 by Auerbach alone).
